faqs.q: How long does a central heating installation take?
faqs.a: A full central heating installation in a 3-bedroom semi-detached property typically takes 3-5 days. Larger properties or complex layouts take longer.

faqs.q: How many radiators do I need?
faqs.a: A qualified heating engineer calculates the heat loss for each room based on size, insulation, window area, and orientation, then sizes radiators accordingly. Undersized radiators are the most common reason homes never get warm enough.

faqs.q: What is a power flush and do I need one?
faqs.a: A power flush forces water and chemicals through your heating system at high velocity to remove sludge and corrosion debris. It's recommended before fitting a new boiler to an old system — debris from old pipes can damage a new boiler within months.

faqs.q: Should I add inhibitor to my heating system?
faqs.a: Yes — inhibitor prevents internal corrosion and sludge buildup, extending the life of your boiler and pump significantly. It should be added to all new installations and refreshed every 2-3 years.

localParagraph: Central heating in WestTulipham presents a varied set of considerations for homeowners, largely due to the area's mixed housing stock and its location within South Lanarkshire. Properties across WestTulipham range from older stone-built homes to more modern developments, meaning boiler requirements, pipe configurations, and system compatibility can differ considerably from one street to the next. The region's mixed water hardness is worth noting, as it can contribute to limescale accumulation within boilers and heat exchangers over time, gradually reducing efficiency if systems are not properly maintained or protected with an appropriate inhibitor. Homeowners in both older and newer properties would benefit from periodic power flushing and annual servicing to keep systems running reliably, particularly through the colder months. Selecting a heating engineer who understands the specific demands of South Lanarkshire's housing mix will ensure that any installation, repair, or upgrade is carried out with the right materials and approach for the property in question, delivering reliable warmth and long-term value.
whatItInvolves: Central heating installation or replacement involves fitting a new boiler, radiators, pipework, and controls to heat your home efficiently. A full system installation is a major project typically taking 3-5 days. A system upgrade — replacing radiators and adding smart controls to an existing boiler — takes 1-2 days. Both must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
process: Survey: calculate heat loss per room and size radiators accordingly. First fix: run new pipework routes, fit radiator brackets, position boiler location. Second fix: hang radiators, connect boiler, fit programmer and thermostatic radiator valves. Commission: fill system, add inhibitor, balance radiators for even heat distribution, test all controls. Register with Building Control. Full system flush prior to filling removes debris that causes cold spots and pump failure.
whatToExpect: A full central heating installation in a 3-bed semi takes 3-5 days. You'll be without heating and hot water during the works — plan around this in winter. Modern systems with smart thermostats (Nest, Hive, Tado) can reduce heating bills by 20-30% through accurate scheduling. Your installer should provide a full commission certificate and Building Regulations notification.
